assessment_summary: The statement claims that every regular edge-transitive graph is vertex-transitive. This is false. A graph that is regular and edge-transitive but not vertex-transitive is known as a semi-symmetric graph. The smallest such graph is the Folkman graph, which is 4-regular and has 20 vertices. Its automorphism group acts transitively on its edges but has two distinct orbits on its vertices (the two bipartite halves), meaning it is not vertex-transitive.
counterexample: The Folkman graph (a 4-regular bipartite graph on 20 vertices). It is edge-transitive but not vertex-transitive, making it a semi-symmetric graph.
